usage: forge-init <name> <description> [<repo>=<description>...]
Run 'forge-init --help' for details.

Usage: forge-init <name> <description> [<repo>=<description>...]

Set up forge in the current directory: a workspace whose direct
subdirectories are git repos, or a single-repo project (a workspace of
one). Safe to rerun: adds new repos and missing docs, never overwrites a
doc, and re-renders every router. Never creates, changes or reads a
CLAUDE.md; Claude Code loads .claude/rules/*.md alongside it.

Arguments:
  <name>                  project name, the router's heading
  <description>           one line: what the project is
  <repo>=<description>    one line: what a child repo is; required for a
                          repo without a rendered router, which otherwise
                          keeps its line

Reads:
  */.git                  each direct subdirectory holding one is a child repo
  <repo>/.claude/rules/forge.md
                          a rendered repo router keeps its description line
  <repo>/PRODUCT.md DESIGN.md
                          linked from that repo's router when present
  vault/Index.md <repo>/vault/Index.md
                          linked from that router when present
  $FORGE_TEMPLATES/       doc and router templates
                          (default ~/.claude/forge/templates)

Writes:
  .git                    git init, when the root is not a repo
  .gitignore              one /<repo>/ line per child repo
  .claude/rules/forge.md  the workspace router
  .forge/                 PROJECT RULES REJECTED STATE todo seeds; tracks/;
                          a single repo also gets the repo docs below
  <repo>/.claude/rules/forge.md
                          the repo router
  <repo>/.forge/          STACK INTEGRATIONS CONVENTIONS TESTING
                          ARCHITECTURE CONCERNS RULES REJECTED

Example:
  cd ~/Projects/acme
  forge-init acme "Acme apps." web="The web app."
